tagline: A leading Japanese cryptocurrency exchange and marketplace platform
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of verified accounts is the primary indicator of user penetration and loyal customer base within the crypto ecosystem, and represents the fundamental driver of transaction and service revenue growth.

kpis.name: Verified Accounts
kpis.explanation: Total number of customer accounts that have completed identity verification (KYC). Each verified user corresponds to a unique customer account.
kpis.description: As of March 31, 2025, Coincheck had over 2.3 million verified users. This metric is adjusted for closed accounts but does not include inactive accounts. Approximately 51% of accounts are held by customers under 40 years old.
kpis.signal: Strong user base growth despite crypto market volatility.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from all company activities, primarily from the Marketplace platform.
kpis.description: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, total revenue was 383,330 million yen (approximately 383.3 million USD). 99.6% of revenue comes from transactions on the Marketplace platform. Growth was driven by Bitcoin's rise to a record high of 17,041 thousand yen in January 2025.
kpis.signal: Very strong growth driven by rising Bitcoin prices and increased trading activity.

kpis.name: Marketplace Trading Volume
kpis.explanation: Total value of transactions executed on the Marketplace platform during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, Marketplace trading volume was 337.5 trillion yen. Over 90% of users access the platform via the mobile app.
kpis.signal: Recovery in trading volume linked to rising cryptocurrency prices and increased platform activity.

kpis.name: Customer Assets
kpis.explanation: Total value of cryptocurrencies and fiat currencies held on behalf of customers (calculated under Japanese generally accepted accounting principles).
kpis.description: As of March 31, 2025, customer assets amounted to 859 billion yen. This metric includes cryptocurrencies and fiat currencies deposited by customers, but excludes NFTs. Customer assets are determined under Japanese accounting principles (J-GAAP).
kpis.signal: Increase in customer assets reflecting growing interest in Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit excluding non-recurring items related to business combination and Nasdaq listing.
kpis.description: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, Adjusted EBITDA (excluding items related to business combination and listing) was 5,718 million yen. Unadjusted EBITDA was a loss of 12,603 million yen due to exceptional charges.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement in adjusted operating result despite net loss, due to adjustment of exceptional expenses.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net profit or loss after all expenses and taxes under IFRS accounting standards.
kpis.description: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, net loss was 14,350 million yen, compared to net profit of 1,967 million yen the prior year. This deterioration was due to non-recurring charges (business combination and listing costs), not operational decline.
kpis.signal: Loss reported due to significant charges related to business combination and Nasdaq listing.

risks.title: Critical dependence on crypto prices and volumes
risks.score_rationale: Risk ranked first in Item 1A with quantified data (98.9%-99.6% of revenue). Intense language ("substantially dependent", "adversely affected"). Stable but structural trend. Dominant weight: crypto volatility directly tied to business model.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and security breaches of customer assets
risks.score_rationale: Major dedicated section (3 pages) with recent concrete examples (DMM Bitcoin May 2024: 48.2 trillion yen, Bybit February 2025: 1.5 billion USD). Highly intense language ("sophisticated", "state actors", "DPRK-affiliated"). Trend up: increasing geopolitical threats. Critical weight: reputation and regulatory compliance.

risks.title: Geographic concentration on Japanese retail market
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned: "dependent on Japanese retail customers who account for nearly all of the trading volume". Clear language ("particularly vulnerable"). Stable but structural trend. High weight: lack of geographic diversification limits resilience.

risks.title: Regulatory risks and multi-jurisdictional compliance
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Item 1A: "changes to any laws or regulations in the United States, Japan or the Netherlands" and "administrative sanctions, including fines". Moderate language but strict regulatory context in Japan (JFSA). Trend up: new wallet rules in response to hacks. High weight: costly compliance.

risks.title: Intense competition and market share loss
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited: "ability to compete and increase market share in a highly competitive industry". Moderate language but clear competitive context. Stable trend. Medium-high weight: differentiation through asset types, speed, fees, security.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party providers and service disruptions
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned: "interruptions in services provided by third-party service providers" and "system failure or outages, including with respect to our crypto platforms or other third-party crypto networks". Moderate language. Stable trend. Medium weight: operational and reputational impact.

risks.title: Regulatory classification risks of crypto assets
risks.score_rationale: Cited: "status of any particular crypto asset as to whether it is deemed a security in any relevant jurisdiction". Moderate language but potentially significant impact. Stable trend but latent risk. Medium weight: affects product offerings.

risks.title: Operational risks related to NFT Marketplace
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned: "legal, regulatory, and other risks in connection with Coincheck's operation of the Coincheck NFT Marketplace". Moderate language. Stable trend. Medium weight: secondary revenue segment but growing regulatory exposure.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the provided documents. The company's strategy appears focused on expanding its Marketplace and Exchange platforms, improving governance, and managing risks following its acquisition by Monex in 2018.
evidence: No reference to AI or machine learning in the documents
Cited innovations relate to the NFT Marketplace, IEOs, and enhanced security measures
No mention of predictive analytics or AI-based automated services
